ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $C$ and $D$ are points on $\odot O$, $\angle CDB=25^\circ$. A tangent to $\odot O$ passing through point $C$ intersects the extension of $AB$ at point $E$. What is the measure of $\angle E$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line OC,\\
$\because$ CE is the tangent to $\odot$O,\\
$\therefore$ OC$\perp$CE,\\
which means $\angle$OCE$=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$COB$=2\angle$CDB$=50^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$E$=90^\circ-\angle$COB$=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is circle ⊙O, AB is a horizontal diameter, and O is on AB; B is on the right side of the circle, and E is to the right of B and is located on the extension of AB. Point C is on the upper right of the circle; the line CE drawn through C is tangent to the circle and intersects the extension of AB at E; point D is on the lower right of the circle, and CD and DB are connected in the figure. Reasoning: Draw radius OC. Because CE is the tangent to circle ⊙O at point C, radius OC is perpendicular to tangent CE, that is, ∠OCE=90°. It is known that ∠CDB=25°, and it is an inscribed angle subtending the same arc CB; the corresponding central angle ∠COB=2∠CDB=2×25°=50°. Also because O, B, E are collinear, and E is on the extension beyond B, ray OE has the same direction as OB, so ∠COE=∠COB=50°. In right triangle OCE, ∠E=90°−50°=40°.
